title: FastGlioma Visual Foundation Model Detects Residual Brain Tumor Infiltration in Under 10 Seconds
whyItMatters: Published in Nature: detects microscopic glioma infiltration in fresh brain-surgery tissue in <10 seconds (92.1% AUROC across 220 international patients), beating MRI and 5-ALA fluorescence head-to-head.
summary: Neurosurgeons and AI researchers led by Todd Hollon (University of Michigan) and Shawn Hervey-Jumper (UCSF), with NYU and the Medical University of Vienna, developed FastGlioma in Nature—an open-source visual foundation model pretrained via self-supervision on ~4 million rapid, label-free stimulated Raman histology images. In a prospective, multicenter international cohort of 220 diffuse glioma patients, FastGlioma quantified microscopic tumor infiltration in fresh surgical tissue in under 10 seconds with 92.1 ± 0.9% AUROC, outperforming standard image-guided and 5-ALA fluorescence surgical adjuncts by a wide margin in a head-to-head prospective study (n = 129) while generalizing zero-shot to pediatric brain tumors.
technicalHighlights: Pretrained on ~4 million label-free optical microscopy images to score microscopic glioma infiltration in fresh surgical tissue in <10 seconds.
Achieved 92.1 ± 0.9% AUROC across a prospective, multicenter international cohort of 220 patients across WHO molecular subtypes.
Dramatically outperformed standard MRI navigation and 5-ALA fluorescence in a head-to-head prospective study (n = 129) and generalized zero-shot to pediatric brain tumors.
caveats: Requires intraoperative stimulated Raman histology imaging hardware in the operating room; randomized survival-outcome trials evaluating long-term patient progression-free survival are ongoing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Establishes real-time label-free optical foundation models as a transformative surgical guidance paradigm in oncology.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly addresses the #1 driver of early glioma recurrence—missed microscopic tumor margins—and extends zero-shot to pediatric brain tumors.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature with prospective, multicenter international validation (n = 220) and head-to-head clinical comparison (n = 129).
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivers whole-slide intraoperative pathology guidance in under 10 seconds without tissue staining or frozen-section delays.

sources.label: Kondepudi, Hervey-Jumper, Hollon et al. — Foundation models for fast, label-free detection of glioma infiltration (Nature, 2024/2025)
